data.title: Narrative Amplified by a Coordinated Cluster
data.summary:
A cluster of accounts amplified campaign content at a volume and rhythm inconsistent with
organic sharing, saturating the conversation around the organisation's name.
data.description:
Flooding does not need to persuade. Filling the available space around a search term or
hashtag displaces other material, and an audience that encounters only one account of
events treats it as consensus.

The distinguishing features are the amplification ratio — accounts that share far more
than they originate — and reciprocity, where the same accounts amplify each other across
unrelated topics. Volume alone is not evidence; genuine outrage also produces volume.

Flooding has a measurable effect on the organisation's own reach, and quantifying that
displacement makes the impact concrete in a way that reach figures for the campaign do
not.
data.recommendation:
* Quantify the displacement of the organisation's own content, not only the campaign's
  reach; it is the impact that matters.
* Report the cluster as a network, with reciprocity evidence, rather than account by
  account.
* Maintain communication through channels the organisation controls, which cannot be
  flooded.
data.short_recommendation: Quantify displacement; report the cluster as a network.
